page.title: Channels
page.purpose: The catalogue of every channel this install could use, ordered by how much work each one takes, with unavailable ones shown as a prompt to satisfy their requirement rather than as options that fail three screens later.

priorities.statement: Which channels can be attached right now, on this host
How much setup each one actually takes, before starting
Why an unavailable channel is unavailable, and what would fix it
Which attached channels are healthy and which have stopped working
Which capabilities are a paid convenience rather than a locked feature

states.description: Available channels are listed first, ordered by declared setup friction.
Availability is being computed from host facts.
No descriptor loaded, which is a configuration fault and is stated as one.
Availability for some channels could not be computed; those are marked unknown rather than available.
Availability is cached; its age is stated.
The catalogue could not be read; a retry is offered.
The signed-in person may not attach channels.

claims.statement: Available channels appear in ascending order of the setup friction their descriptor declares.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-013. Ordering is derived from data so a new channel lands in the right place by arriving.

claims.statement: A channel whose requirements are unmet is never presented as a selectable attach action.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-012. Letting somebody start an attach that cannot finish is the worst outcome on this page.

claims.statement: An unavailable channel names the unmet requirement and links to the action that would satisfy it.
A channel whose availability could not be computed is perceivably distinct from one known to be available.
claims.rationale: Treating unknown as available produces exactly the dead end the previous claim forbids.

claims.statement: Setup effort is legible before the attach action is used, not discovered during it.
A gated channel states that it is a paid convenience and that the same capability is available with the operator's own credentials.
claims.rationale: The monetisation contract forbids gating a capability a self-hoster could run themselves; the surface has to say so.

claims.statement: At most five channels are shown before the show-all action, so the screen never becomes a decision-paralysis list.
Every per-channel label, limit and capability shown on this page is read from the descriptor.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-002. If the console hardcodes a channel name, the descriptor stopped being the source of truth.

claims.statement: An empty catalogue is presented as a configuration fault naming the descriptor directory, not as an ordinary empty state.
Availability and health states stay distinct in both themes.

regions.purpose: Channel descriptors with availability computed from host facts.
